items.detail: SemanticFusion [24] recently demonstrated how a dense 3D reconstruction obtained by SLAM can be enriched with semantic information. This work, and other similar papers such as [25], add semantics to the map _after_ it has been created and do not fully leverage the relationship between geometry and semantics. The maps are not object-centric, but rather dense point clouds, where every point carries a semantic label, or a distribution over labels. In contrast, our approach uses objects as landmarks inside the SLAM system and the resulting map consists of objects encoded as quadrics.

items.summary: Kernel Fusion and Memory Optimizations in High-Performance Gaussian Splatting Pipelines
items.detail:
Consolidating execution steps into fused CUDA kernels and leveraging specialized GPU memory hierarchies (registers, shared memory, and asynchronous copies) drastically reduce CPU-GPU roundtrip overhead and memory contention in 3D/2D Gaussian Splatting.

Modern Gaussian Splatting systems address execution bottlenecks by fusing optimization updates and rasterization operations directly onto GPU hardware. Techniques such as fused backward optimizer kernels (Faster-GS, Taming 3DGS, Pattern P8) compute parameter gradients and update Adam moments within GPU registers, eliminating global memory roundtrips and CPU-GPU synchronization latency. Furthermore, managing thread synchronization via warp-level reduction primitives, shared memory array buffering (HTGS, diff-gauss), and asynchronous data prefetching (cuda::memcpy_async) mitigates atomicAdd collisions and global bandwidth limitations. Note that specific latency and throughput gains vary across GPU architectures, and full empirical profiling remains context-dependent.

evidence.title: II Related Work
evidence.text: SemanticFusion [24] recently demonstrated how a dense 3D reconstruction obtained by SLAM can be enriched with semantic information. This work, and other similar papers such as [25], add semantics to the map _after_ it has been created and do not fully leverage the relationship between geometry and semantics. The maps are not object-centric, but rather dense point clouds, where every point carries a semantic label, or a distribution over labels. In contrast, our approach uses objects as landmarks inside the SLAM system and the resulting map consists of objects encoded as quadrics.

evidence.title: Kernel Fusion and Memory Optimizations in High-Performance Gaussian Splatting Pipelines
evidence.text:
Consolidating execution steps into fused CUDA kernels and leveraging specialized GPU memory hierarchies (registers, shared memory, and asynchronous copies) drastically reduce CPU-GPU roundtrip overhead and memory contention in 3D/2D Gaussian Splatting.

Modern Gaussian Splatting systems address execution bottlenecks by fusing optimization updates and rasterization operations directly onto GPU hardware. Techniques such as fused backward optimizer kernels (Faster-GS, Taming 3DGS, Pattern P8) compute parameter gradients and update Adam moments within GPU registers, eliminating global memory roundtrips and CPU-GPU synchronization latency. Furthermore, managing thread synchronization via warp-level reduction primitives, shared memory array buffering (HTGS, diff-gauss), and asynchronous data prefetching (cuda::memcpy_async) mitigates atomicAdd collisions and global bandwidth limitations. Note that specific latency and throughput gains vary across GPU architectures, and full empirical profiling remains context-dependent.
